clue.text: Scold charwoman?

definitions.meaning: a scold is a nagging, foul-mouthed woman
read as a char's woman: the char is a fish, so its woman is the fish's wife

explanation.surface: Someone tells off the cleaning lady.
explanation.walkthrough: A charwoman is a cleaner, but the question mark invites reading 'char' as the fish of that name.
explanation.definitionFit: A coarse, loud-mouthed woman is called by this name after the brawling women of old fish markets.

clue.text: Like silk in Florence, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the name is said aloud, giving a same-sounding word

parts.note: Flossie is a pet form of the name Florence

explanation.surface: Silk is made in the Italian city of Florence, so we are told.
explanation.walkthrough: Florence looks like the Italian city but is a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Flossy means made of or like floss, the soft silk thread.

clue.text: Diocese was upset, having to move from one extreme to the other

definitions.text: to move from one extreme to the other

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the word upwards, so it reads backwards

explanation.surface: A diocese was in turmoil, swinging between extremes.
explanation.definitionFit: To seesaw is to swing back and forth between opposites, like a playground plank.

clue.text: Pleasure might require self-control

parts.note: will means pleasure or wish, as in at His pleasure
power means might, strength

explanation.surface: Indulging in pleasure might need restraint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might' looks like the verb; it is the noun meaning strength.
explanation.definitionFit: Willpower is the strength of mind to restrain impulses, a synonym for self-control.

clue.text: Treatment one believes may make one better

definitions.text: Treatment one believes may make one better

parts.words: Treatment one believes may make one better
parts.note: a cure that works, if at all, through the patient's belief in it

explanation.surface: A remedy that works only if the patient trusts it.
explanation.definitionFit: This practice claims to cure through prayer and belief rather than medicine.

clue.text: Beetle back from pub, since clubs are closed up

indicators.note: back says the whole string of pieces is read from its end to its start

parts.note: a bar is a pub

indicators.note: the clubs are shut in, enclosed by the word for since

parts.note: as means since, because
C is the abbreviation for clubs, the card suit

explanation.surface: Someone retreats from the pub because the clubs have shut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are closed up' reads as shut-down clubs but signals the enclosure; 'back' turns the whole run, and 'from' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The scarab is a dung beetle, sacred in ancient Egypt.

clue.text: Fine earthenware for a friend

definitions.meaning: porcelain, the delicate ware for cups and plates
Cockney rhyming slang, ... plate meaning mate, a friend

explanation.surface: Good crockery bought as a present for a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: In Cockney rhyming slang 'china plate' rhymes with mate, so a china is a pal.
explanation.definitionFit: The porcelain is named after its country of origin, and the slang shortens china plate, rhyming with mate.

clue.text: Left-wing Thespian and literary organiser

parts.note: red means left-wing, socialist
a thespian is an actor

explanation.surface: A socialist actor also edits books.
explanation.definitionFit: A redactor is an editor who prepares and arranges texts for publication.

clue.text: Dispose of body near the cemetery

indicators.note: to dispose is to arrange, so these letters are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: Get rid of a corpse close to the graveyard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dispose of' looks like getting rid of the body, but it rearranges BODY NEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Boneyard is an informal word for a graveyard.

clue.text: Covered on top, with round face

parts.note: over means on top of

indicators.note: round says the next word's synonym is turned about

parts.note: a dial is a clock's face

explanation.surface: Something is covered over the top and has a round face, like a clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' reads as describing a clock's face, but it signals a turnaround.
explanation.definitionFit: Overlaid means covered with a layer laid over the top, a synonym.

clue.text: Refuse heap in centre of animal's lair

parts.note: mid means in the centre of
a den is a wild animal's lair

explanation.surface: A rubbish heap sits in the middle of some beast's den.
explanation.definitionFit: A midden is a dunghill or rubbish heap, especially an ancient one dug up by archaeologists.

clue.text: Sort of store to go mad in

parts.note: depart means to go
mental is slang for mad

explanation.surface: A shop is enough to drive one mad.
explanation.definitionFit: A department store sells many kinds of goods in separate sections.

clue.text: Hair producer wants to resell theatre tickets

definitions.meaning: the skin of the head, from which hair grows
a ticket tout resells tickets at inflated prices, a verb sense

explanation.surface: The producer of the musical Hair is caught touting tickets for it.
explanation.walkthrough: The italic 'Hair' suggests the stage musical, which suits the theatre tickets.
explanation.definitionFit: The skin of the head grows hair, and in British slang to tout tickets above face value is also this verb.

clue.text: Superior-sounding man is for priestly government

indicators.note: sounding says the words are said aloud to give the answer's sound

parts.note: higher means superior; said aloud it gives the opening sound
Archy is a man's name, a form of Archibald

explanation.surface: A self-important man belongs to the government of priests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Superior-sounding' reads as snooty, but its sound signal covers only the word for superior; the man's name follows as written.
explanation.definitionFit: The word first meant rule by priests, a ranked order of clergy, before its general sense of a ranking.

clue.text: Pudding with tart sauce

parts.note: sweet is the British word for pudding or dessert
and means with, together with
tart means sour in taste

explanation.surface: A dessert comes with a sharp-tasting sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tart' looks like a pastry beside the pudding, but it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A sauce of sugar and vinegar common in Chinese cookery is called by this name.

clue.text: You're in a tricky position here, where you can't touch base

definitions.text: You're in a tricky position here, where you can't touch base

parts.words: You're in a tricky position here, where you can't touch base
parts.note: a place too deep to stand in, and also the idiom for being in trouble

explanation.surface: In trouble and out of one's depth, unable to reach the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in this place means being in serious trouble, and literally water too deep to stand.

clue.text: Pots deer, perhaps -— a worthless activity

parts.note: mugs are drinking pots
deer are an example of game animals

explanation.surface: Someone shoots at deer, which turns out to be futile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pots' looks like a verb, as in shooting game; it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A mug's game is British slang for a pointless or foolish undertaking.

clue.text: They affect the voice of Addison in broadcast about English

indicators.note: about says the rearranged letters go around the next piece
broadcast means scattered, so these letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: Something affects Addison's voice when he speaks on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts E inside ADNOIDS, an anagram of ADDISON signalled by 'broadcast'.
explanation.definitionFit: Adenoids are throat tissue whose swelling gives a nasal voice.

clue.text: Briefs junior counsel, at first unwilling to accept points

parts.note: under means junior, lower in rank

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of counsel

parts.note: loth is a spelling of loath, unwilling
E and S are compass points

explanation.surface: A junior barrister is briefed, though reluctant at first to take on points of law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Briefs' and 'counsel' suggest lawyers' instructions; it is underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Briefs are underpants, one kind of underwear.

clue.text: Heartless chief in charge of boxing

indicators.note: heartless removes the central letter of the word

parts.note: first means chief, foremost

explanation.surface: A cruel boss directs the boxing.
explanation.definitionFit: Fistic means relating to fists, so to fighting with them.

clue.text: See fish round ship or boat

parts.note: V is the abbreviation for vide, Latin for see

indicators.note: round says the fish surrounds the ship

parts.note: an eel is a fish
SS is the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: Look at the fish swimming round the ship or boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel is any ship or boat.

clue.text: Judgment about first person to show awareness

indicators.note: about says the word for judgment goes around the next piece

parts.note: a sentence is a judge's judgment
I is the first person pronoun

explanation.surface: A judge's ruling on the first person shows sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Sentience is the capacity to feel or perceive, a kind of consciousness.

clue.text: Gambling, daughter lost white coat

indicators.note: lost says the daughter is taken out

parts.note: dicing is gambling with dice

explanation.surface: After gambling, a daughter lost her white coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'white coat' suggests a doctor's coat; it is the sugar coating on a cake.
explanation.definitionFit: Icing is the white sugar coating spread over a cake.

clue.text: Dispense with spoken farewell, perhaps

indicators.note: spoken says the word is said aloud, giving a same-sounding word

parts.note: a wave is one way of saying goodbye

explanation.surface: Someone skips the spoken goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: To waive a right or rule is to forgo it, dispensing with it.

clue.text: Tart sick at heart after drug

indicators.note: after places the heart of sick behind the drug

parts.note: acid is slang for LSD

indicators.note: at heart takes the middle letters of sick

explanation.surface: A tart feels ill deep down after taking drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tart' looks like a person; it is the adjective meaning sour.
explanation.definitionFit: Acidic means sharp and sour in taste, like vinegar.

clue.text: Note in standing regulations

indicators.note: in puts the note inside the word for standing

parts.note: status means standing, social position
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A note appears among the standing rules.
explanation.definitionFit: Statutes are laws passed by a legislature, formal regulations.

clue.text: Most ginseng treatment is standard.

indicators.note: treatment says the remaining letters are worked over into a new order
most says the word loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Most ginseng therapy is routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most' drops the final G of ginseng; 'treatment' rearranges GINSEN.
explanation.definitionFit: An ensign is a flag, and a standard is a flag too.

clue.text: Such a life Eliot depicted, describing office work

definitions.meaning: George Eliot wrote Scenes of ... Life, about the lives of clergy
the adjective for clerks' desk work

explanation.surface: Eliot's novel described a life of office drudgery.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means relating to clergy, as in Eliot's title, and also to clerks and office work.
